description: RHW landmark extraction finds landmarks by working back from the goal. A *landmark* is a fact, or a set of facts of which one must hold, that is true at some point of every plan. For each landmark it looks at the *possible first achievers*: the operators that add it and that can run before it holds. A precondition that all of them share is a new landmark; preconditions on one variable can form a *disjunctive* landmark; and values that every path through a variable's domain transition graph passes are landmarks too. It also records the orderings between landmarks (greedy-necessary, natural and reasonable), which LAMA-style search uses.

papers.authors: Silvia Richter, Malte Helmert, Matthias Westphal
papers.title: Landmarks Revisited
